stories.headline: Ship struck near Strait of Hormuz and oil rebounds 3%, undercutting Trump's talks claim

key_facts.fact: A cargo vessel was struck by an unidentified projectile near the Strait of Hormuz off Oman's coast early on Tuesday, August 4, according to the UKMTO maritime security agency; maritime sources said it was a dry bulk ship whose crew had to abandon it, with one seafarer missing.
key_facts.excerpt: a cargo vessel reported being struck by an unidentified projectile near the Strait of Hormuz off Oman's coast, according to the UKMTO maritime security agency... Maritime sources told Reuters on Tuesday that the vessel struck near Hormuz was a dry bulk ship. Its crew had to abandon the vessel and one seafarer was missing

key_facts.fact: Oil prices rose nearly 3% on Tuesday, reversing part of Monday's selloff that had taken Brent crude futures down about 7% to a three-week low on Trump's upbeat comments about diplomacy.
key_facts.excerpt: Oil prices rose nearly 3% after a steep selloff in the previous session as investors reassessed optimism over diplomacy... Brent crude futures had fallen about 7% to a three-week low on Monday after Trump's upbeat spin on diplomacy, but analysts cautioned that the move appeared premature.

key_facts.fact: Qatar's Foreign Ministry said efforts to resolve the US-Iran conflict are 'in very progressive stages' and that drafts of a potential agreement are 'being circulated', but that there are no direct talks between the two sides.
key_facts.excerpt: Efforts to resolve the US-Iran conflict are "in very progressive stages," Qatar's Foreign Ministry said, adding that drafts of a potential agreement are "being circulated" but that there are no direct talks between the two sides.

key_facts.fact: Iran's stated goal in its talks with Oman is 'temporary arrangements' lasting up to three months under which Tehran would control a route through the strait.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's goal in its talks with Oman "is to set temporary arrangements" — lasting up to three months — where Tehran can control a route through the strait.

key_facts.fact: Trump said on Monday that talks were under way and that the Strait of Hormuz would be 'completely open' by Tuesday as 'phase one', with a second phase covering Iran's nuclear program; Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said there were no negotiations with the United States.
key_facts.excerpt: "We're talking about the strait, the opening of the strait, having it open literally by tomorrow, completely open, and that's phase one," Trump said... "We currently do not have negotiations with America," and Iran has no plans to host foreign delegations or send negotiators abroad in the coming days, Foreign Affairs Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei told reporters.

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said it is still enforcing the blockade of Iranian shipping and has redirected 44 commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz since reimposing the measure in mid-July.
key_facts.excerpt: US Central Command (CENTCOM) says it's continuing to enforce the blockade against Iran and has redirected 44 commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz since it reimposed the measure mid-July.

stories.headline: Pentagon signs $3B framework deals with Northrop to triple Patriot and quadruple THAAD output

key_facts.fact: Northrop Grumman signed two multi-year framework agreements totaling over $3 billion with the US Department of War, announced on August 3: a $2 billion deal for PAC-3 MSE solid rocket motors and ignition safety devices, and a $1 billion deal for THAAD components, each spanning seven years.
key_facts.excerpt: Northrop Grumman (NYSE: NOC) has signed two multi-year framework agreements totaling over $3 billion... Under the $2 billion framework agreement, the company will supply essential components, including solid rocket motors and ignition safety devices... The $1 billion framework agreement will enable Northrop Grumman to significantly increase monthly deliveries of THAAD components over seven years.

key_facts.fact: The deal makes Northrop a second supplier of PAC-3 rocket motors, ending L3Harris's position as sole producer of solid rocket motors for the interceptor.
key_facts.excerpt: Northrop Grumman will become a second supplier of rocket motors for the in-demand PAC-3 interceptor while also increasing motor production for THAAD missiles... L3Harris is currently the sole producer of SRMs for PAC-3.

key_facts.fact: Defense officials said the agreements support a long-term procurement objective of nearly 14,000 Patriot and THAAD interceptors, tripling PAC-3 MSE capacity and quadrupling THAAD capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: Defense officials said the agreements are intended to support the department's long-term procurement objective of nearly 14,000 Patriot and THAAD interceptors by providing sustained demand signals to critical suppliers throughout the defense industrial base.

key_facts.fact: Northrop will raise PAC-3 MSE motor output at its Allegany Ballistics Laboratory in Rocket Center, West Virginia, supporting an Army plan to grow annual PAC-3 MSE production from roughly 600 units today to thousands.
key_facts.excerpt: Since 2021, the company has doubled its production capacity for tactical solid rocket motors at ABL and plans to triple production capabilities by 2027. This investment supports the U.S. Army's growth in annual PAC-3 MSE missile production from roughly 600 units today to thousands in the near term

key_facts.fact: The agreements follow a Center for Strategic and International Studies estimate that the US has burned through roughly two-thirds of its Patriot and THAAD stockpiles since the Iran war began, and come days after Lockheed Martin announced a contract modification of up to $53.86 billion for PAC-3, bringing the multiyear total to $58.62 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: a recent Washington-based think tank assessment that said the U.S military has spent significant portions of its Patriot (PAC-3) and THAAD stockpiles since the beginning of the Iran war earlier this year... On Wednesday, Lockheed announced a government award of up to $54 billion to accelerate its Patriot missile production.

key_facts.fact: Since the start of the year the Pentagon has signed about a dozen framework agreements with defense companies to boost munitions production, including for Tomahawk cruise missiles, solid rocket motors and seekers.
key_facts.excerpt: Since the beginning of the year, the Pentagon has signed about a dozen framework agreements with defense companies to boost production rates for in-demand munitions like the Tomahawk cruise missile and for key components like solid rocket motors and seekers.

stories.headline: Ukrainian drones hit Moscow-region industrial site and more Wildberries depots, killing five

key_facts.fact: A drone strike early on August 4 on the Novoselki industrial zone in Chekhov, about 69 km south of the Kremlin in the Moscow region, killed five people and wounded 10, regional governor Andrei Vorobyov said.
key_facts.excerpt: At least five people were killed and 10 more injured at an industrial site about 69km (43 miles) south of the Kremlin, local officials said... Moscow region governor Andrei Vorobyov said a warehouse was hit and caught fire, at an industrial site in Chekhov on the outskirts of Moscow

key_facts.fact: Two warehouses of Wildberries, Russia's largest online retailer, were hit overnight in the Tver and St Petersburg regions; Robert Brovdi, commander of Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces, said Ukrainian drones have attacked 15 Wildberries logistics facilities in three weeks and 13 were destroyed by fire.
key_facts.excerpt: Early on August 4, Wildberries' warehouses in the Tver and St Petersburg region were hit... Robert Brovdi, commander of Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces (USF), said on social media that Ukrainian drones have attacked 15 logistics facilities belonging to Wildberries over the past three weeks. He added that 13 of the 15 warehouses had been destroyed by fire as a result of the attacks.

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian drones also struck the Syzran oil refinery in Russia's Samara region, with geolocated footage showing black smoke rising from the facility, according to media reports and the OSINT channel ASTRA.
key_facts.excerpt: According to media reports and Telegram channel ASTRA's OSINT analysis, Ukrainian drones also struck the Syzran oil refinery in Russia's Samara region, with geolocated footage showing black smoke rising from the facility.

key_facts.fact: Russia's defence ministry said it intercepted and destroyed 320 drones overnight; Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 136 drones at Ukraine, of which 117 were shot down or intercepted.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia's defence ministry said it had intercepted and destroyed 320 drones overnight.

key_facts.fact: Russian strikes killed at least five civilians in Ukraine: six guided aerial bombs on Sumy killed two girls aged 5 and 10 and an elderly woman, and an 89-year-old woman was killed in the port city of Mykolaiv.
key_facts.excerpt: "Two children and an elderly woman were killed in Russian (guided aerial bomb) strikes on Sumy tonight," Oleg Grygorov said on Telegram. "The girls were 5 and 10 years old."... Another attack on the port city of Mykolaiv in southern Ukraine killed an 89-year-old woman

key_facts.fact: The death toll from Monday's drone strike on the crowded beach at the Black Sea resort of Arkhipo-Osipovka rose to seven, including children, with 58 wounded and 21 hospitalized, Krasnodar regional authorities said on Tuesday.
key_facts.excerpt: The death toll from a drone strike Monday in the Russian Black Sea resort of Arkhipo-Osipovka rose to seven, including four children, regional authorities said. On Tuesday morning, Krasnodar regional authorities updated the number of wounded to 58, with 21 of them hospitalized.

stories.headline: Curium to buy Lantheus for up to $8B on a day of more than $14B in pharma and medtech deals

key_facts.fact: Curium and Lantheus Holdings announced a definitive merger agreement on August 3 under which Curium US will pay $102.50 per share in cash plus contingent value rights worth up to $12.00 per share, for total consideration of up to $114.50 per share and an aggregate transaction value of up to approximately $8.0 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Curium US will acquire all of the outstanding shares of Lantheus for $102.50 per share in cash at closing, plus non-transferable Contingent Value Rights ("CVRs") providing for up to $12.00 per share in potential additional cash payments... a total per share consideration of up to $114.50 and a total transaction value of up to approximately $8.0 billion.

key_facts.fact: The price represents a 38% premium to Lantheus's unaffected 60-day volume-weighted average price as of May 21, 2026, and the deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027; the combined radiopharmaceutical company would serve oncology, neurology and cardiology patients in more than 70 countries.
key_facts.excerpt: representing a premium of 38% to Lantheus' unaffected 60-day volume-weighted average price... Combined company would serve oncology, neurology and cardiology patients across more than 70 countries... The transaction is currently expected to close in the first half of 2027

key_facts.fact: Also on August 3, Supernus Pharmaceuticals and Indivior Pharmaceuticals agreed to an all-stock merger of equals creating a CNS company with pro forma net revenue of $2.2 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $888 million and $125 million in expected annual cost synergies; Indivior shareholders will receive a $1.0 billion special cash dividend and own about 56.5% of the combined company.
key_facts.excerpt: The combined company is expected to generate pro forma net revenue of $2.2 billion and pro forma adjusted EBITDA of $888 million... Indivior Pharmaceuticals stockholders will receive a one-time special cash dividend of $1.0 billion in aggregate immediately prior to closing... Indivior Pharmaceuticals stockholders will own approximately 56.5% of the combined company

key_facts.fact: The combined Supernus will hold 11 marketed CNS products, be listed on Nasdaq under 'SUPN', and is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, with a $650 million Citibank term loan financing the dividend.
key_facts.excerpt: merging into one central nervous system–focused company with a whopping 11 marketed products in the space... To pay the $1 billion dividend, the companies secured a $650 million Citibank loan... The deal has been approved by both companies' boards and is slated to close in the fourth quarter of this year.

key_facts.fact: The same day, KKR agreed to take medical-device contract manufacturer Integer Holdings private for $5.7 billion, and AstraZeneca shares fell about 7% after reports it had explored a roughly $400 billion tie-up with Bristol Myers Squibb.
key_facts.excerpt: KKR agreed to acquire Integer Holdings, a global contract manufacturer of medical-device components, in a $5.7 billion deal, according to both Reuters and Bloomberg... Reports that AstraZeneca had explored acquiring Bristol Myers Squibb in a deal that could have been valued at roughly $400 billion sent AstraZeneca shares down about 7%

stories.headline: Otsuka's VOYXACT halts kidney decline in IgA nephropathy over two years in Phase 3 VISIONARY

key_facts.fact: Otsuka announced on August 3 that the Phase 3 VISIONARY trial met its key secondary endpoint, with an annualized eGFR slope of +0.3 mL/min/1.73 m2/year (95% CI, -0.4 to 0.9) for sibeprenlimab versus -4.2 (95% CI, -4.9 to -3.6) for placebo over 24 months.
key_facts.excerpt: Phase 3 VISIONARY study met its key secondary endpoint, showing an annualized estimated eGFR slope of +0.3 (95% CI, -0.4 to 0.9) mL/min/1.73 m²/year with sibeprenlimab versus -4.2 (95% CI, -4.9 to -3.6) mL/min/1.73 m²/year with placebo

key_facts.fact: The treatment effect was +4.5 mL/min/1.73 m2/year (95% CI, 3.6 to 5.4; p<0.0001) at 24 months, and VOYXACT is described as the first IgA nephropathy treatment to reach the KDIGO goal of halting kidney function decline to a physiologic rate of under 1 mL/min/1.73 m2/year.
key_facts.excerpt: demonstrating a statistically significant treatment effect of +4.5 (95% CI, 3.6 to 5.4; p<0.0001) mL/min/1.73 m²/year at two years (24 months). VOYXACT is the first IgAN treatment to achieve the KDIGO therapeutic goal of effectively halting progressive kidney function decline to physiologic rate (<1 mL/min/1.73 m²/year for most adults)

key_facts.fact: Safety over two years was comparable to placebo, with overall adverse events of 90.7% versus 90.0%, infections 51.4% versus 51.0%, and serious infections lower on sibeprenlimab at 1.9% versus 4.0%; no new safety signals were identified.
key_facts.excerpt: similar rates of overall adverse events (90.7% vs 90.0%), infections and infestations (51.4% vs 51.0%), and injection site reactions (35.1% vs 32.2%). No new safety signals were identified, and rates of serious infections were lower with sibeprenlimab than placebo (1.9% vs 4.0%)

key_facts.fact: The results were presented in a late-breaking oral presentation at the GlomCon Hawaii 2026 conference and complete the VISIONARY dataset feeding Otsuka's rolling supplemental BLA submission to the FDA for traditional approval.
key_facts.excerpt: Results presented during a late-breaking oral presentation at the GlomCon Hawaii 2026 conference... These new findings complete the Phase 3 VISIONARY study dataset, marking another milestone in Otsuka's rolling submission of a supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA) to the U.S. FDA for VOYXACT traditional approval.

key_facts.fact: VOYXACT (sibeprenlimab-szsi) is a humanized monoclonal antibody blocking APRIL, dosed as a self-administered subcutaneous injection every four weeks, and received FDA accelerated approval on November 25, 2025 based on proteinuria reduction.
key_facts.excerpt: VOYXACT (sibeprenlimab-szsi) is a humanized monoclonal antibody that binds to and blocks APRIL... VOYXACT is a self-administered, subcutaneous injection dosed once every four weeks... VOYXACT was granted accelerated approval by the U.S. FDA on November 25, 2025.

stories.headline: Hughes files for Chapter 11 after satellite broadband subscribers fall 22% to Starlink

key_facts.fact: Hughes Satellite Systems Corporation and certain US subsidiaries, including Hughes Network Systems, filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in the US Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas, Houston Division, announced on August 3.
key_facts.excerpt: Hughes Satellite Systems Corporation... today announced that it and certain of its U.S. subsidiaries, including Hughes Network Systems, LLC, have filed voluntary chapter 11 petitions in the Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas, Houston Division

key_facts.fact: Court filings show Hughes lacked the cash to repay roughly $1.5 billion of debt that matured on August 1, with an August 3 deadline.
key_facts.excerpt: according to filings with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas, Hughes lacked the cash needed to repay about $1.5 billion of debt by an Aug. 3 deadline.

key_facts.fact: Chief restructuring officer Robert Del Genio said in a court filing that Hughes broadband subscribers fell roughly 21.7% over the past year to around 641,000 amid competition from low Earth orbit operators, and that the company does not expect the trend to reverse.
key_facts.excerpt: The filing cites that HughesNet subscribers have declined about 22% over the past year to 641,000 broadband subscribers. "The company does not expect this trend to reverse," Del Genio said... Del Genio cited the impact of SpaceX's Starlink and Amazon Leo.

key_facts.fact: EchoStar's broadband and satellite services revenue fell 6.7% year over year to $317 million in the quarter ended June 30, and Hughes lost 59,000 net broadband customers in Q2 versus 34,000 a year earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: It lost 59,000 net broadband customers in Q2, up from 34,000 a year ago... Wireless service revenue dipped 0.3% to $929 million, while satellite broadband revenue fell 6.7% to $317 million.

key_facts.fact: The reorganization is meant to accelerate a shift from residential satellite broadband to enterprise, government and defense customers, where Hughes says it has a $1.5 billion contracted backlog; parent EchoStar and Hughes' international subsidiaries are not part of the filing, and DISH TV, Sling TV and Boost Mobile are unaffected.
key_facts.excerpt: accelerate its ongoing transformation into an enterprise, government, and defense-focused business... EchoStar Corporation ("EchoStar") and Hughes' international subsidiaries are not included in the chapter 11 proceedings... including DISH TV, Sling TV, and Boost Mobile.

key_facts.fact: It is the third EchoStar-related bankruptcy in recent weeks, after Dish DBS and Dish Wireless filed in July; unlike Dish DBS's prepackaged restructuring, Hughes entered Chapter 11 without a creditor deal already agreed.
key_facts.excerpt: which come a month after parts of EchoStar's business tied to satellite TV and its abandoned 5G network filed for bankruptcy protection... Unlike the prepackaged restructuring for DISH DBS, Hughes entered Chapter 11 without a deal already agreed with creditors.

stories.headline: Polymarket in early talks to raise about $1B at a valuation above $20 billion

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported on August 4 that Polymarket is in early talks with prospective investors to raise about $1 billion at a valuation of more than $20 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Polymarket is seeking to raise capital at a valuation of more than $20 billion... The prediction-markets platform is in early talks with prospective investors to raise about $1 billion, according to people familiar with the matter

key_facts.fact: The round would value Polymarket at more than twice the $9 billion it fetched in October 2025, and would follow an April 2026 round at a $15 billion valuation whose close had not previously been reported.
key_facts.excerpt: If it closes the round, Polymarket will be worth more than twice as much as it was in October 2025, when it raised money at a valuation of $9 billion... Polymarket completed a round at a $15 billion valuation in April, when it brought in D.E. Shaw and venture capital firm G Squared as new investors

key_facts.fact: The April round totaled about $1 billion, including a $600 million investment from Intercontinental Exchange, the owner of the New York Stock Exchange, alongside existing backers SV Angel, Dragonfly and Valor Equity Partners.
key_facts.excerpt: That round... also saw existing backers SV Angel, Dragonfly and Valor Equity Partners add to $600 million from Intercontinental Exchange Inc., reaching a total of about $1 billion.

key_facts.fact: Rival Kalshi said in May that a new investment valued it at $22 billion and has far outpaced Polymarket's growth since the start of the year as Polymarket ran into operational and legal issues.
key_facts.excerpt: The firm's chief rival, Kalshi, said in May that it had secured a new investment that pegged its value at $22 billion. Kalshi has far outpaced Polymarket's growth since the beginning of the year as Polymarket ran into operational and legal issues.

key_facts.fact: Polymarket has posted more than $1.2 billion in annualized revenue since launching its US platform, but Kalshi is handling three times more trading volume and a CFTC investigation is under way.
key_facts.excerpt: Polymarket has posted more than $1.2 billion in annualized revenue since launching its US platform, but rival Kalshi is handling three times more trading volume and a CFTC investigation is underway.
